item: Trending counts and corpus_keywords are read in short statements (read-chunking)
summary: trending()._counts reads its date window as one short statement per day per 10,000-keyword-id range (windowed_group_counts) and corpus_keywords reads its article set 100 articles at a time and adds the sums, instead of one GROUP BY open for the whole read; same answer and key order (property tests), rowid bound at the start so rows inserted above it are not counted (not one snapshot: a re-used rowid is counted, an article re-indexed during the read can be missing; both pinned), keep runs only between statements; a checkpoint passes between statements on a real WAL file and on the app's engine. Dense synthetic 1.75M rows: total time about the same, longest statement 0.09-0.15 s down to under 5 ms; on a sparse key span (1.32M mentions over 3M ids) trending_windows is 7.3 s in 42,618 statements against 2.6 s for the single statements (about 110 us a statement; 8.2 to 9.0 s with the pool slot given back after each key range, 1,723 check-outs), several days in one IN list was refused (a planner scan with the country filter). Each range's connection goes back to the pool (not on a snapshot session), a datetime bound is read as the single statement, and a row moved by a keyword fold during the read can be counted twice. The seeks go through the session's connection so the briefing's WAL guard keeps nothing per seek. A session holding a real write transaction, a read_only_db session (one BEGIN on purpose) and emergence.py are out of its reach.
